text:
Maya Patel: Quick pass on the new latency card — Figma link: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/latency-v2 :eyes:
Tom Nguyen: thanks — looks cleaner. main worry is p95 label overlap when range is narrow
Li Wei: +1 on overlap. can we collapse the p95 chip into an icon on narrow widths?
Maya Patel: maybe. but icon needs tooltip and accessible name. prefer explicit label for screen readers
Harper Kline: for screen readers we can add `aria-label=\"p95 latency (95th percentile)\"` and keep visible text optional
Tom Nguyen: also noticing heatmap row density feels 'jagged' — users confuse it with missing data
Maya Patel: true. propose smoothing and a subtle dotted grid background to imply sampling
Li Wei: agree. what about sampling controls copy — right now it says `Show samples` which is vague
Harper Kline: suggestion: `Sampling scope` with a sublabel `Auto | Per-request | Full` — clearer for users
Maya Patel: love that. update copy to: `Sampling scope — Auto (recommended)` by default
Tom Nguyen: small a11y nits: keyboard focus order on the time range picker jumps after the apply button
Maya Patel: repro steps plz
Tom Nguyen: open picker, TAB across presets, SHIFT+TAB back to calendar, focus lands on Apply then back to presets (should be linear)
Maya Patel: filed a quick issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/UX-1234
Design Bot: Snapshot saved for 1719269999 — baseline v2-heatmap-annotate
Li Wei: tiny CSS tweak for p95 chip when collapsed:

```
.p95-chip[aria-hidden=\"true\"] { width: 28px; text-indent: -9999px; }
.p95-chip[aria-hidden=\"true\"]::after { content: \"95%\"; text-indent: 0; }
```

Maya Patel: probably better to use `aria-label` instead of hiding text; avoid visually hidden hacks
Harper Kline: agree. final decision: keep visible 'p95' on desktop, collapse to an icon+aria-label under 420px, add heatmap smoothing, update sampling copy to `Sampling scope`, fix keyboard order — I'll mock and share tomorrow :thumbsup:
